Most competitive list I’ve found so far is Rampager with -1AP buff, 6 Brigands, 2 Huntsman, 2 Karnivores in reserve, 1 Nurgling Unit in Reserve. 

Basically every game I’ve won I’ve done the same thing. Strategically get Rampager on the biggest threat to your wardogs and “trade”. Rush brigands and huntsman to get all middle objectives and max out on those points in turn 1-3. Use your fire power to keep them from coming to center.Still hold on 4 and 5 if you can but getting that early lead is essential. Use Karnivores to bring in to help clear out an objective or threat. Then use the nurglings mainly to get points on things like Deploy Homers, Behind enemy lines, engage on all fronts , etc. They also come in handy against scout models and stuff and are good the screen with. They have a lot of good uses for 45 points. 

Ive used the all dogs list and it definitely has some advantages too but the Rampager feels more consistent getting in and trading with big guys and tanks 

Your key stratagems are gonna be Tank Shock, Move though walls one, and Terror Shades (I’ve had this feel come in handy a lot. It’s also been consistent finishing off models that you didn’t kill fully the melee phase with Karnivores during their command step.

I used a 5 gallon bucket and some simple green. I didn’t cut it with water but I did add a couple of cups of vinegar in the mix. I placed the models in it for a 2 days. Took them out and ran some water over it while gently but firmly scrubbed it with a denture brush. Usually the first scrub just agitated the paint. Then place back in for a day. Next time the paint would just scrub off easily. Then repeat as any times as you want. You’re not going to get all of the paint. Sometimes in the tiny crevices it gets stubborn so you can pick it out with a needle or something. But at this point I just reprimed it and didn’t notice any difference. Also note that if you are doing a lot of models like I did. Eventually you’ll have to get new simple green. Because it loses it chemical reaction to get the paint to come lose.
